title: Foods to Limit or Cook Thoroughly During Pregnancy
excerpt: Food-safety guidance inspired by CDC/NHS/FDA themes: deli meats, unpasteurized dairy, high-mercury fish, and undercooked foods.
content:
## Introduction
When pregnant, it's essential to choose safe and healthy foods to ensure the well-being of both mother and baby. In this article, we'll provide information on foods that pregnant women should limit or cook thoroughly to avoid health risks.

## Foods to Limit
According to the CDC, NHS, and FDA, pregnant women should limit the following foods:

* Deli meats and hot dogs: These foods can contain Listeria, which can cause health problems for mother and baby.
* Unpasteurized dairy products: Unpasteurized dairy products can contain Salmonella and E. coli, which can cause health problems for mother and baby.
* High-mercury fish: High-mercury fish like shark, swordfish, and king mackerel can contain mercury, which can harm the development of the baby.
* Undercooked foods: Undercooked foods like sushi, sashimi, and raw eggs can contain Salmonella and E. coli, which can cause health problems for mother and baby.

## Foods to Cook Thoroughly
To ensure food safety, pregnant women should cook the following foods thoroughly:

* Meat and poultry: Cook meat and poultry to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to ensure that bacteria are killed.
* Eggs: Cook eggs to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to ensure that bacteria are killed.
* Seafood: Cook seafood to an internal temperature of at least 145°F (63°C) to ensure that bacteria are killed.

## Practical Tips
Here are some practical tips to help pregnant women choose safe and healthy foods:

* Read food labels: When buying food, read the labels to ensure that the product has been pasteurized and does not contain bacteria.
* Cook food thoroughly: Cook food to the recommended internal temperature to ensure that bacteria are killed.
* Avoid undercooked foods: Avoid undercooked foods like sushi, sashimi, and raw eggs to reduce the risk of health problems.

## When to Seek Help
If pregnant women have any questions or concerns about food safety, they should consult their doctor or a registered dietitian. They can provide specific information and advice to help pregnant women choose safe and healthy foods.

## Conclusion
Food safety is crucial during pregnancy. Pregnant women should limit or cook thoroughly foods like deli meats, unpasteurized dairy products, high-mercury fish, and undercooked foods. Read food labels, cook food thoroughly, and avoid undercooked foods to reduce the risk of health problems. If you have any questions or concerns, consult your doctor or a registered dietitian.
